# CV Website — Copilot Instructions

## Project Overview
This is a **Hugo static site** that renders a professional CV from a single YAML data file. The site is designed with a minimalist business-card aesthetic, accessibility compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA), and clean black-and-white print output.

## Architecture

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `assets/data/cv.yaml` | **Canonical CV content** — the base; edit this file first |
| `assets/data/cv.*.yaml` | Tailored variants (e.g. `cv.canonical-frontend.yaml`) — generated by the job-fitness-review skill, synced via cv-variant-sync |
| `content/{slug}.md` | One content page per variant; front matter `dataFile` param points to its YAML |
| `assets/css/main.css` | Screen stylesheet (CSS custom properties, BEM naming) |
| `assets/css/print.css` | Print/PDF stylesheet (A4 optimised, B&W safe) |
| `themes/cv-card/layouts/partials/cv-body.html` | Shared CV rendering partial (reads `dataFile` param) |
| `themes/cv-card/layouts/index.html` | Home page — delegates to `cv-body.html` partial |
| `themes/cv-card/layouts/_default/single.html` | Variant pages — same delegation pattern |
| `themes/cv-card/layouts/_default/baseof.html` | Base HTML shell (head, skip-link, footer) |
| `hugo.toml` | Hugo configuration |
| `.gitea/workflows/deploy.yml` | CI/CD: build → PDF → deploy via rsync (Gitea Actions) |
| `.github/skills/job-fitness-review/SKILL.md` | Skill: analyse job fitness, generate tailored variant YAMLs |
| `.github/skills/cv-variant-sync/SKILL.md` | Skill: propagate base CV edits to all variant files |

## Key Conventions

- **Data-driven**: CV content lives in `assets/data/`. The canonical base is `cv.yaml`; variants follow the `cv.{slug}.yaml` naming pattern. Templates must never contain hardcoded CV text.
- **Variant system**: Each variant is a full copy of `cv.yaml` with tailored summary, skill ordering and highlights. A matching `content/{slug}.md` exposes it at `/{slug}/`. The `cv-body.html` partial reads the `dataFile` front-matter param to select the YAML.
- **Single-page site**: Only `index.html` and variant content pages exist. Hugo taxonomies and sections are disabled.
- **CSS methodology**: BEM naming (`block__element`), CSS custom properties for theming. No CSS frameworks.
- **Accessibility**: All sections use `aria-labelledby`, icons are `aria-hidden`, a skip-link is present, focus styles use `outline`, and colour contrast meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 minimum).
- **Print-first colour choices**: The palette is intentionally neutral/greyscale so the CV retains its character when printed in B&W. Avoid introducing colours that don't degrade well to greyscale.
- **No JavaScript**: The site is pure HTML + CSS. Do not add JS unless explicitly requested.
- **Inline styles**: CSS is inlined via Hugo's `readFile` for single-request page loads. Do not use `<link>` stylesheet references.

## How to Edit the CV
1. Open `assets/data/cv.yaml` (the canonical base — always edit here first)
2. Edit any section (personal, experience, education, skills, languages, certifications, interests)
3. Run `hugo server` to preview, or push to `main` to trigger CI/CD
4. After editing the base, use the **cv-variant-sync** skill to propagate relevant changes to any variant files (`assets/data/cv.*.yaml`)

## Build Commands
```bash
hugo server          # Local dev server with live reload
hugo --gc --minify   # Production build → public/
```

## PDF Generation
The CI/CD pipeline generates a PDF using headless Chrome (`--print-to-pdf`). Locally you can do:
```bash
hugo --gc --minify
chrome --headless --print-to-pdf=public/cv.pdf --print-to-pdf-no-header public/index.html
```
The print CSS (`assets/css/print.css`) controls PDF layout: A4 page size, 15mm/18mm margins, hidden footer, and URL expansion for links.

## Deployment
The CI/CD pipeline runs on a **self-hosted Gitea instance** using Gitea Actions (`.gitea/workflows/`). The workflow uses plain shell commands (no GitHub marketplace dependencies) to install Hugo, build the site, generate a PDF via headless Chromium, and deploy via rsync over SSH.

Required Gitea repository secrets (Settings → Actions → Secrets):
- `DEPLOY_HOST` — server hostname or IP
- `DEPLOY_USER` — SSH username
- `DEPLOY_KEY` — private SSH key (ed25519 recommended)
- `DEPLOY_PATH` — remote directory (e.g. `/var/www/cv`)

Gitea Actions is largely compatible with GitHub Actions YAML syntax but third-party marketplace actions may not be available. Prefer shell commands over action references when modifying the pipeline.

## When Modifying Templates
- Keep the semantic HTML structure: `<header>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<dl>` for skills
- Every `<section>` must have an `aria-labelledby` pointing to its `<h2>` id
- Test both screen and print rendering after changes
- Run `hugo --gc --minify` to verify there are no build warnings
